sentences.text:
-------Respondents
For Petitioner : Mr. Sabyasachi Bhaduri, Advocate For State : Mr. Vinay Pandey, Dy. Adv. General
Hon'ble Shri Parth Prateem Sahu, Judge Order On Board 10 / 07 /202 4
1.
Petitioner has filed this writ petition seeking following reliefs.
"10.1 to set aside the impugned memo(s) dated 01.06.2020 passed by the Ld. Land Acquisition Officer/ Sub-Divisional Officer (Revenue), Raipur.
10.2 To issue appropriate writ/ writs directing the respondents to calculate and disburse the interest amount against the remaining compensation amount paid to the petitioner on 07.03.2020.
10.3 Any other relief(s) in favour of petitioner as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper under the facts and circumstances of the case."

2. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that the land owned by petitioner measuring 230 sq.m.
and 58.55 sq.m. bearing khasra No. 1552/1(d) situated at village Gudhiyari, was acquired for the purpose of 'railway under bridge'.

Amount of compensation was also calculated, however, initially only 80% of the awarded amount was released in his favour and remaining 20% of the amount was Jawahar Daga vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164640659/

entities.text: Jawahar Daga vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The succession case filed was decided in favour of petitioner and thereafter balance amount of 20% was also released, but without any interest.

Petitioner filed an application under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act and the Collector referred the case to the District Judge, wherein the claim of petitioner with respect to the interest was rejected.
He submits that as there is delay in payment, petitioner is entitle for interest under Section 34 of the Land Acquisition Act.

3. Learned State counsel raised objection with regard to maintainability of the writ petition on the ground that the claim of petitioner with respect to interest is considered by Fourth Additional District Judge, Raipur and has rejected the claim and therefore the petitioner is having other efficacious remedy to challenge the order of the District Judge before appropriate forum.
4. The submission made by learned State counsel is not disputed by the counsel for petitioner that the petitioner is having other remedy of appeal against the order of Additional District Judge.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.

6. Taking into consideration the nature of grievance raised, facts and circumstances of the case and submission made by learned counsel for the parties that the petitioner is having other efficacious remedy of appeal, I am not inclined to entertain this writ petition.
7. Accordingly, the writ petition is dismissed reserving liberty to petitioner to avail other efficacious remedy available to him under the law.

Sd/-
